title: When the Aftermath Turns
premise: Cyrus Marchetti, a night librarian drifting through a sleepless city, is asked by Odile Vasseur — the last fluent speaker of a dying language called Lumençal — to become her final student before her memory fails entirely. As their lessons deepen into an unlikely found family that includes Odile's estranged granddaughter Noor and the library's ragged night regulars, Cyrus discovers the language holds an untranslatable word for 'goodbye said properly,' and that Odile has been saving it for someone she wronged decades ago. When Odile's health collapses mid-lesson, Cyrus must choose between cataloguing her recordings for the archive (duty) or helping her finish the one conversation she never dared to have. The novel ends with Odile's death at dawn, the word finally spoken aloud by all of them together, and Cyrus signing their name to a life they finally own.
about_author: Xanthe Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing endangered-language recordings in coastal university libraries. They write quietly devastating fiction about people who keep things — words, objects, promises — for others.

chapters.title: The Hours That Belong to No One
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. We meet the night library: insomniacs, a man sleeping in periodicals, Cyrus's careful habit of belonging nowhere. A letter arrives requesting the archive room after hours. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for peace, cracked open by curiosity.

chapters.title: A Woman Made of Verbs
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Odile Vasseur arrives at 2 a.m., sharp and funny, and asks not for books but for a student. She tests Cyrus with sounds no alphabet holds. Emotional beat: reluctant wonder; Cyrus agrees to one lesson, telling themselves it means nothing.

chapters.title: Lumençal
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. The first real lesson: the language names light, grief, and bread with terrifying precision. Noor appears, hostile, convinced Cyrus is exploiting her grandmother. Emotional beat: the pleasure of learning collides with guilt over wanting something this much.

chapters.title: What the Archive Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Noor watches her grandmother laugh in a way she hasn't seen since childhood, and resents it. Flashbacks to the family rupture. Emotional beat: jealousy curdling into fear that there isn't time left to repair anything.

chapters.title: The Word for Goodbye Said Properly
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Odile teaches the untranslatable word — a farewell that releases both speaker and listener — but refuses to say who it was meant for. Her first lapse in memory happens mid-sentence. Emotional beat: dread entering the warm room; stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Found People
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating close-third among the night regulars. The library becomes a household: lessons spill into shared meals, the sleeping patron learns greetings, Noor starts recording too. Emotional beat: the quiet joy of chosen family forming without anyone admitting it.

chapters.title: The Recording
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus finds an old tape in which young Odile says the goodbye-word to someone named Elias — and realizes the person she owes it to died believing he was never forgiven. Duty says archive everything; love says help her finish. Emotional beat: the central choice sharpened.

chapters.title: Everything Falls at Once
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Odile collapses during a lesson; the university moves to seize the recordings as institutional property; Noor and Cyrus clash over what Odile would want. Emotional beat: climax of external pressure — family, bureaucracy, and mortality converging on one small room.

chapters.title: Said Out Loud
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, her only chapter. Fragile, luminous, half-dreaming, she dictates the proper goodbye — to Elias, to Noor, to the language itself — while Cyrus and Noor speak it back to her, word by word, until it is truly out loud. Emotional beat: catharsis; release after a lifetime of holding.

chapters.title: Owner
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, months later. Odile dies at dawn off-page; the community wins the archive fight and opens a free listening room in her name. Cyrus signs a lease, keeps teaching two students, and says the word properly at her grave. Emotional beat: grief integrated; a tenant becomes an owner of their own life.
